title: Within-visit systolic pressure decline fails to improve transferred handgrip prediction beyond mean hemodynamics and body size
abstract: We tested whether the difference between the first systolic cuff reading and the mean of the next two predicts concurrent handgrip strength beyond conventional measures. Sex-specific spline models trained in NHANES 2011–2012 (n=3605) were frozen and evaluated in separately recruited NHANES 2013–2014 (n=4013). Adding a flexible systolic-decline term increased examination-weighted MSE from 127.7225 to 128.3416 kg²: delta +0.6191, joint source/target PSU-bootstrap 95% interval [-0.2532, +2.6635]. The registered improvement criterion failed. Adjustment for arm circumference and comparison against within-visit systolic SD did not produce favorable point differences. This exploratory negative result does not exclude other information in blood-pressure dynamics, establish equivalence, or validate an autonomic biomarker. Transfer across recruitment cohorts in one survey program is not external-program confirmation.
